findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is an endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance term and no affinity-head derivative.

The information audit is a geometric nearest-teacher versus Hungarian fixed-frame RMS comparison over 14 independent batches; it explicitly is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and its nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect.

Compressed-choice excess fixed RMS is small (whole-window mean about 0.081 A, CI95 roughly 0.070-0.092) while top4 teacher overlap is only about 0.47, so selection enrichment relative to the fixed-frame reference is modest and should not be read as an absolute geometric descriptor of affinity.

Terminal credit is available only as parent-debiased survival moments and a compact credit table over 14 complete-survival batches, with multiple testing applied jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests; these are survival/quality credits, not terminal affinity effects.

Ancestral coverage is thin: 349 of 700 batch nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit and the terminal-affinity comparison is unavailable.

Continuous contrast features are observed-node linear fits with extrapolation disallowed and no accepted polynomial; several landmark features show large first-to-last rate reversals (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass first_rate_z about +9.3 to last_rate_z about -10.0) with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts, so a constant rule is not supported over the observed window.

Curve support is restricted to 24 selected features under a fidelity rule requiring relative RMSE <= 0.35, zero strong sign-conflict nodes and quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1, with selection requiring absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857 and q < 0.05; this is a filtered subset, not the full feature population.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant coordinate contrast weighting
hypotheses.falsifier: a selected feature whose observed-node contrast is constant in sign and magnitude within fit fidelity, or a time-conditioned rule that fails to improve over the constant rule on held-out batches
hypotheses.observable: validated observed-node contrast curve for a selected landmark feature
hypotheses.scope: observed score window [0.0, 0.5], selected curve-support features only
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention rule using validated observed-node contrast changes may outperform a constant static regional rule, because landmark contrast features reverse sign across the observed window rather than holding a fixed direction.

hypotheses.direction: treat selection enrichment as a modest geometric contrast, not an affinity proxy
hypotheses.falsifier: an independent batch set showing high chosen-teacher score correlation with the same selection rule
hypotheses.observable: compressed chosen-teacher score correlation and top4 teacher overlap
hypotheses.statement: Selection enrichment at observed nodes is only weakly aligned with teacher score (compressed chosen-teacher score correlation about 0.10), so a coordinate rule that assumes strong score alignment would be over-claiming.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record and survival credit cannot be interpreted as final affinity benefit.
The information audit is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and its excess-distance metric is nonnegative by construction, so it is not a causal affinity effect.
Continuous trend fits are observed-node linear with extrapolation disallowed and no accepted polynomial; no arbitrary time bins or extrapolation are used.
Turnover, moment, pair-kernel and joint-motif diagnostics were not read in this pass and are not claimed here.
No current-study outcome data are available to this role.
